TOPIC:
Review Updated 2026-2027 Textbook Selection and Adoption Proposal

POLICY ALIGNMENT:
IIAA, Textbook Selection and Adoption
IIAA-R, Textbook Selection and Adoption Regulation

BACKGROUND:
This supports the key priority of the division’s strategic plan Elevate '28 and provides WJCC teachers
and students access to current, aligned textbooks and textbook materials. The board previously
approved an adoption process and timeline that included CTE and Mathematics. World Languages
has been added as an additional content area for adoption.

 PROPOSED COURSES FOR TEXTBOOK SELECTION & ADOPTION
 Course                                          Timeline
 CTE: AP Business & Personal Finance             September – December 2026
 Mathematics: Pre-Algebra 6, Pre-Algebra 7, Pre- September – December 2026
 Algebra 8 and Algebra I
 *World Languages: Spanish I, II, III, IV and AP January – April 2027
                    German I, II, III, IV and AP

Process
The Teaching & Learning and College, Career and Readiness (CCR) departments will lead the
textbook selection and adoption process for each content area in collaboration with review
committees and informed by stakeholder input. The proposal includes the identification of the
textbook evaluation committee, a timeline for the scope of work, and adherence to the guidelines and
criteria outlined in Policy IIAA and Regulation IIAA-R, for each course.

Committee
Each textbook selection committee will include a school board member, division staff, school
administrators, general education teachers, specialists representing content, special education,
multilingual learners, gifted, parents/guardians, and community members.

RATIONALE:
School Board Policy IIAA requires the local school board approve the textbook selection and adoption
schedule, the textbook evaluation committee, and evaluation criteria.

SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A

items.title: Review Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2028 Budget Calendar
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
11/10/2026
TOPIC:
Review Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2028 Budget Calendar Related to Capital Improvement Plan
Development
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
DB, Annual Budget
BACKGROUND:
The state code requires that the school board present a balanced budget, in which revenues equal
expenditures, to the city and county on or before April 1st. The FY28 budget year covers the period from July
1, 2027 through June 30, 2028.
The three primary phases in the budget development process include: 1) Superintendent's Proposed Budget
(administrative recommendation presented to the school board); 2) School Board Proposed Budget (school
board recommendation to the James City County Board of Supervisors and the Williamsburg City Council);
and, 3) School Board Adopted Budget (school board adopted budget based upon funding
authorization/appropriation by the county and city).
The process includes three opportunities to gather community input, one in November to discuss the Capital
Improvement Plan (CIP), one in January prior to the development of the Superintendent's Proposed Operating
Budget and another in February prior to approval of the School Board Proposed Operating Budget.
Williamsburg-James City County Public Schools' personnel will develop the CIP in September and October.
The operating budget development process starts with reviewing departmental and school budget requests
beginning in November using the WJCCPS Strategic Plan to provide direction.
The Superintendent's Proposed Budget is developed and presented to the school board in February. After a
public hearing on the budget, the school board approves the School Board Proposed Budget in March and
refers it to the James City County Board of Supervisors and the Williamsburg City Council for consideration.
The localities must approve the appropriation for the school system no later than May 15th or within 30 days of
the receipt by the county or municipality of the estimates of state funds, whichever occurs later. Based upon
approved funding by the county and city, the school board makes any necessary adjustments and approves an
Adopted Budget in May.
RATIONALE:
The School Board approved the Fiscal Year 2028 Budget Calendar on August 18, 2026. Since that approval,
attendance zone modifications associated with the division's redistricting process were finalized on October 20,
2026. The revised attendance zones affect enrollment projections, capacity analyses, and long-term facility
planning assumptions that are used in development of the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).
In consultation with James City County and the City of Williamsburg, administration recommends adjusting the
FY28 budget calendar to allow sufficient time to incorporate the finalized attendance zones into enrollment



forecasts and CIP recommendations. These revisions will ensure that the proposed CIP reflects the most
current student enrollment and facility planning information prior to School Board consideration.
The following revisions are recommended:
•
•
•
•

Presentation of Superintendent's Proposed Capital Improvement Plan from November 10, 2026 to
January 5, 2027.
Public Hearing on recommended Capital Improvement Plan from November 17, 2026 to January 19,
2027.
Joint Meeting on Capital Improvement Plan and Enrollment from December 4, 2026 to February 5,
2027.
Adoption of the School Board Capital Improvement Plan from December 8, 2026 to February 2, 2027.

The amended FY28 Budget Calendar is included for review.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
Attendance zone modifications associated with the division's redistricting process were finalized on October
20, 2026. Additional time is needed to incorporate the revised attendance zones into enrollment projections
and facility planning analyses that support development of the Capital Improvement Plan. The proposed
amendment does not affect the operating budget development schedule or statutory budget submission
deadlines.
COST BUDGETED:
As presented in budget documents.
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board review the amendment to the Fiscal Year 2028 Budget Calendar
as presented, and be prepared to vote at the November 17, 2026 meeting.
DATA SOURCE:
Daniel Keever, Ph.D., Superintendent
Rene Ewing, Chief Financial Officer

items.title: WJCC Discipline Update
items.body:
TOPIC:
WJCC Discipline Update
BACKGROUND:
In alignment with the Strategic Plan, Elevate Beyond Excellence Bridge to 2028, WJCC Schools continues to
monitor progress of the Key Performance Indicator (KPI) for reducing the percentage of behavioral referrals
that result in suspension from school. This presentation will provide the school board with an update on
division discipline practices, including a report on current discipline data, an overview of the practices and
supports schools use to respond to student behavior, and goals for continued improvement. The update
reflects the division’s commitment to maintaining safe, supportive learning environments while ensuring
discipline is applied consistently across all schools.
RATIONALE:
Updates are provided to the board and public to report on progress, with this presentation focusing specifically
on discipline practices within the Supporting Priority of Safety & Security, including the KPI for reducing the
percentage of behavioral referrals that result in suspension from school. Division staff will report on current
discipline data, review the practices and supports in place across schools, and outline goals and action steps
for the 2026-27 school year.

BACKGROUND:
On October 20, 2026, the School Board approved new school attendance zone boundary maps to take effect
with the 2027-28 school year. Redistricting addresses capacity challenges, particularly at the elementary level,
where eight of the division’s nine schools currently use portable classrooms. The opening of two new pre-K
centers in August 2027 will relocate programs currently housed in five elementary schools, creating
instructional space in some buildings while others are projected to remain at or above capacity. The approved
boundaries support more effective use of available space, feeder pattern alignment, transportation and
operational efficiencies, and the delivery of programs and services across elementary and secondary schools.
An interdepartmental leadership team has developed the WJCC United Transition Roadmap to guide
implementation. The roadmap is organized around four areas of focus: Student Experience, Employee
Experience & Team Transitions, Family Engagement, and Communications & Logistics.
RATIONALE:
Successful implementation requires coordinated planning that addresses operational needs while helping
students, families, and employees navigate change and build connections within their school communities.
This update will provide the School Board and community with a shared understanding of actions completed
and immediate next steps and planned support within the WJCC United Transition Roadmap. Additional
updates will be provided as implementation details are finalized and the roadmap is refined in response to
emerging needs and stakeholder feedback.

items.title: Superintendent’s Transition Plan Report – Phase III Update
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
11/10/2026
TOPIC:
Superintendent’s Transition Plan Report – Phase III Update
BACKGROUND:
Dr. Daniel F. Keever was appointed as the new superintendent of WJCC Public Schools effective July 1, 2025.
Subsequently, his Superintendent’s Transition Plan was developed through a comprehensive and collaborative
process grounded in stakeholder engagement and data analysis. Over the course of more than a year,
including his tenure as interim superintendent, input was gathered from students, staff, families, and
community members through surveys, focus groups, listening sessions, school visits, and community
meetings. This feedback was combined with insights from the Elevate ’28 strategic plan, student outcomes
data, and key performance indicators. By analyzing both perception data and performance data, the plan was
shaped to reflect the shared priorities, needs, and aspirations of the school community. The result is a
transition plan that is student-centered, collaborative, and aligned with the division’s strategic direction.
The Superintendent's Transition Plan is structured into five phases over an 18-month period, allowing for an
intentional approach to implementation, with each phase building on the progress of the previous one. In this
presentation, Dr. Keever will provide an update on the priority action steps completed during Phase III (July
2026-October 2026). The report will highlight progress, key accomplishments, and next steps as the division
moves into Phase IV, reinforcing the division’s commitment to transparency and continuous improvement.
The full publication is available to the public at https://wjccschools.org/about-wjcc/superintendents-transitionreport/.
RATIONALE:
Phase III of the Superintendent's Transition Plan was from July 2026 to October 2026. As noted in the plan,
the superintendent shall provide intermittent updates during School Board meetings to share progress,
highlight key milestones, and outline any necessary course corrections to ensure transparency and reinforce
his commitment to open communication and continuous improvement.

items.title: School Board Evaluation Tool Discussion
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
11/10/2026
TOPIC:
School Board Evaluation Tool Discussion
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
AFA, Evaluation of School Board Operational Procedures
BACKGROUND:
The school board believes the efficiency of board operations directly affects the efficiency of division
operations. Therefore, the board will conduct an annual self-evaluation in December.
RATIONALE:
The evaluation will assess the effectiveness of the school board in the discharge of its role, both individually
and as a board. The following conditions shall apply to the school board self-evaluation process:
• School board members are involved in the development of an instrument by which they will evaluate
themselves.
• The school board evaluation will be completed by individual board members confidentially, and
submitted to the school board chair or designee, for compilation of individual results.
• The school board shall meet, with a quorum of members present, to review and discuss the composite
opinions and total results.
• Each conclusion is supported by rationale and objective evidence.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
Upon completion of the annual process, the school board will consider revisions to the school board selfevaluation process.
